To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Chimney come down on Ashbourne Terrace in the wind?? [DRAFT — not posted yet]

Posting as a neighbour who looked from the pavement, not as an engineer on commission — there is no professional cover behind free advice, so this is observation and general sense only.

At 07:05: about 1.2m of the 41 stack is still standing, leaning towards 43, pots gone, mortar washed out at the base. With 50mph gusts again this afternoon, that could go at any time. At 43 the front roof slope is holed over roughly 2-3 square metres, with debris probably in the front bedroom. There's a stepped crack (zig-zag, following the brick courses) from the bay head to the first floor window cill, 5-10mm wide, and the bay head looks dropped by around 20mm.

Mick — please don't go in at 9 with the props. Propping under a holed roof with a loose stack overhead is the worst place to stand: the floors may be loaded with debris and nobody knows the load path now, and a loft inspection from inside is not sensible. Priya, please don't hand over a key. Propping a ceiling and viewing from the loft gallery wouldn't make anyone safer — the risk is above and around the property, not under it.

The pavement is not closed. The tape is only across the front garden of 43, and there are loose slates on the 43 and 45 gutter line directly over the footway. Please use the other side of the road until the council have closed it properly, especially for the school run to St Dunstan's. The dangerous structures team is reached out of hours on the main council number — they already know, so please ask them to close the footway if it is still open.

Mrs Doherty at 45: whether she stays is not my decision, but I would not sleep in the front room tonight, and I would rather she went to family until 45 has been checked. From the pavement, 45's front elevation looks undamaged and the 41 stack sits on the 41/43 party wall, not on 45 — though I could not see the 43/45 wall itself.

For the builder cousin: terraces are robust in general, but this one is damaged — a different situation.
